title: CoreWeave earnings are breathing new life into the AI trade
excerpt: CoreWeave stock surged after earnings, recovering after weeks of volatility stemming from fears about its bonds and a broader panic in the AI trade.
content_html:
CoreWeave just breathed new life into the AI trade

By Samuel O'Brient

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

CoreWeave is trying to mount a comeback after weeks of stock losses driven by concerns about its debt and a broader panic in the AI trade.

Shares surged on Wednesday after the company reported earnings, lifting fellow neoclouds and the tech sector. Investors were piling back in after Tuesday's sell-off sparked by a hot October inflation report.

The stock was 26% around midday.

Other big moves among neoclouds on Wednesday include:

  • Nebius Group: +18%
  • Applied Digital: +7%
  • IREN Limited: +9%

The broader market rallied as tech mounted a comeback.

Here's where major indexes stood around noon ET:

  • S&P 500: 7,626.95, up 1.4%
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average: 52,337.98, up 0.2% (+106 points)
  • Nasdaq 100: 28,515.51, up 2.79%

CoreWeave's revenue for the third quarter came in above Wall Street's estimates, at $3.66 billion compared to $3.55 billion expected, marking a 168% surge from the previous year. It also raised its guidance for the fiscal year to a range of $13 billion to $13.3 billion, up from $12 billion to $13 billion, signaling continued demand for compute at a time when investors have been fretting over a slowdown in the AI boom.

The spike on Wednesday is a stark departure from weeks of volatility that hammered CoreWeave's stock since October. A panic about its bonds, which saw yields spike and prices drop into distressed territory, drove the stock down 20% in a week.

In its latest earnings report, CEO Michael Intrator said that the company's cost of debt came down in the quarter.

"At the end of Q3, our weighted average cost of debt across our entire business was 7.9%, down 250 basis points year over year. Looking ahead, we will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields. Nor do we need to."

In a post on X, Eric Jackson, founder of EMJ Capital, flagged a bullish detail from the report related to CoreWeave's sprawling GPU network.

"Management laid out a potential second economic life for its GPU fleet. 130,000 GPUs coming off contract in 2027," he wrote. "Another 170,000 in 2028. And potentially ~$10 billion in annualized revenue from recontracting that capacity at today's prices."

That could address a key concern for investors, who have worried that GPU depreciation could be a major headwind for CoreWeave and other AI infrastructure firms. Vinny Daniel, cofounder of Seawolf Capital and an investor made famous by "The Big Short," recently said this issue is a key reason behind his short bet against CoreWeave.

Despite the rally on Wednesday, there remains some lingering uncertainty around the trajectory for CoreWeave and the neoclouds. One major headwind on the horizon could be the elections, with the blue wave hinting at a slowdown in infrastructure development next year when Democrats take power in Congress next year.

Some have also raised concerns about heightened competition from the hyperscalers, which are building their own infrastructure and chips to use themselves and offer to AI customers.

"Our experts suggest that declining inference costs could drive even greater demand for computing capacity," noted Garrett Waters, an analyst at market research firm Third Bridge. "That doesn't necessarily mean CoreWeave will capture all of that growth, particularly as hyperscalers continue building out their own infrastructure and deploying custom AI accelerators in-house.

塞缪尔·奥布莱恩 (Samuel O'Brient) 是一位经验丰富的金融市场和商业记者，撰写的文章涉及经济、技术和公共政策等广泛主题。 在《商业内幕》中，他报道了重要的宏观和微观经济故事，包括顶尖经济学家和对冲基金经理的观点、首次公开募股失败、企业破产、迷因股票和卖空。 他还撰写有关加密货币、石油和房地产等其他市场的文章。他采访了许多市场上最有影响力的声音，从马克·赞迪和理查德·塞勒等顶级经济学家到丹尼·摩西、安德鲁·莱夫特、安东尼·斯卡拉穆奇、路易斯·纳维利尔和格兰特·卡登等著名投资者。福克斯的 LiveNOW、Taking Stock 和 Ticker News 等节目让塞缪尔讨论股市和经济发展。 他的报道曾被纽约时报 DealBook、彭博电台、福布斯、Entrepreneur、Gizmodo 和 TheFutureParty 引用。Samuel 最初在 InvestorPlace 工作，报道投资、零售交易和宏观经济趋势。 在加入 Business Insider 之前，他曾担任 TheStreet 的技术市场记者。 他毕业于莎拉·劳伦斯学院和都柏林三一学院。Samuel 的作品曾发表在 TipRanks、EV 和 Observer 等出版物上。 当他不追寻故事时，人们经常会发现他在逛书店和唱片店。 要联系 Samuel，请发送电子邮件至 sobrient@insider.com 或通过 LinkedIn 与他联系。 他还在《信号》中饰演塞缪尔·克莱门斯。
